conventions.slug: Primary page the correction applies to. null for ledger-only corrections that are not page-scoped.
conventions.affectsSlugs: Every page whose published HTML changes when this correction is applied.
conventions.target: content | ledger — which file the field path addresses.
conventions.field: Path into the target. content: pages[i].<path> (e.g. pages[3].lead, pages[1].sections[2].bullets[4], pages[2].faqs[1].answer). ledger: ledger:<SOURCE-ID> for an entry, or ledger:DOCUMENT-LEVEL for a note that sits outside a single entry.
conventions.claimType: verified-fact | inference | hypothesis | editorial. Describes the strength of the reason for the change, not of the proposed wording.

conventions.verification: How the item is closed. runtime-test items must not be published as fact until the test is recorded.
conventions.applyWith: Other correction ids that touch the same string; apply them together to avoid clobbering.

corrections.claimDetail: Verified fact: the exported alpha is the model's subject-segmentation probability and the code contains no ink or darkness threshold, so Clearcut does not perform document thresholding. Hypothesis: what the model actually selects for a photographed signature (the sheet, the ink, or the whole frame) is unknown until a recorded runtime test exists. The proposed wording states only the caution and never asserts which outcome occurs.
corrections.currentText: Need a clean handwritten signature without grey paper behind it for PDFs, digital letters, or invoices? Clearcut isolates dark ink on plain paper locally in your browser memory and exports a watermark-free transparent or white-background PNG—without uploading your signature to a server. Before editing for an Indian exam form, check whether your portal requires a white-paper JPG instead of a transparent PNG.
corrections.proposedText: Need a cleaner signature image for PDFs, digital letters, or invoices? Clearcut separates the photographed sheet or signature area from its surroundings locally in your browser memory and exports a watermark-free PNG on a transparent, white, or coloured background—without uploading your signature to a server. How much of the paper is removed depends on your photo: ink-only transparency is not guaranteed, so preview against a dark background swatch, inspect the exported PNG, and refine with the Erase and Restore brushes; for guaranteed ink-only transparency, use a scanner or a dedicated threshold tool. Before editing for an Indian exam form, check whether your portal requires a white-paper JPG instead of a transparent PNG.
corrections.verification: runtime-test: in desktop Chrome run Standard and Detailed on (a) an A4 sheet with a signature photographed on a contrasting desk and (b) a tight signature crop. For each, record source pixel dimensions, mode, date, model id and the exported PNG alpha histogram (share of fully transparent vs fully opaque pixels). Publish any ink-isolation claim only if the recorded output shows ink-shaped transparency. Until then keep the cautious wording above.

evidence.note: alphaCanvas writes the model probability straight to the alpha channel (pixels.data[offset+3] = Math.round(alpha*255)); smoothstep(0.08,0.92,...) in fast mode only. No darkness or ink threshold exists anywhere in vendor/bg0/.
Models are studioludens/birefnet-lite-512 (98,484,532 bytes) and naddy24/birefnet-512-webgpu (473,435,223 bytes) — general salient-object segmentation networks, not document scanners.
The page already says Clearcut uses a general subject-segmentation network rather than document contrast thresholding; the removed lead sentence contradicted it.

corrections.appliedText: Need a cleaner signature image for PDFs, letters or invoices? You can try Clearcut's on-device background remover and save a PNG without uploading your signature. It uses a general subject-segmentation model: removing only the paper around thin ink strokes is not guaranteed. Check the result against a dark background, inspect the exported PNG, and use Erase or Restore where needed. A dedicated scanning or threshold tool may be a better fit for ink-only transparency. For exam forms, first check whether editing is allowed and whether the portal requires a white-paper JPG.

corrections.claimDetail: Same basis as R1-a: the removed phrase (ink strokes with alpha opacity) asserts an outcome the model is not proven to produce. The replacement describes what a transparent PNG is without promising ink-only cutouts.
corrections.currentText: A transparent PNG keeps only your ink strokes with alpha opacity around them, so your signature sits naturally over PDF lines, Word or Google Docs letters, e-invoices, and certificates without covering underlying borders with a white rectangle.
corrections.proposedText: A transparent PNG keeps the part of the image Clearcut keeps, with transparency around it, so a signature can sit over PDF lines, Word or Google Docs letters, e-invoices, and certificates without covering borders with a white rectangle. Clearcut's models are general subject-segmentation networks rather than document scanners, so the result depends on how your signature is framed and lit: preview against a dark background swatch, inspect the exported PNG, and refine with the Erase and Restore brushes.

evidence.note: Alpha is the model mask; no ink threshold.

corrections.appliedText: A PNG can store transparent pixels, allowing a cutout to sit over a document without a rectangular backdrop. corrections.claimDetail: Verified fact: the refinement pass is skipped whenever the detected subject crop occupies 85% or more of the frame (or is under 32px on either axis). Inference: a tightly cropped signature is likely to fall in that skipped range, because how much of the frame the mask covers depends on what the model selects — so the wording says 'may not run' rather than asserting it.
corrections.currentText: Open Clearcut on desktop Chrome or Edge and upload, drop, or paste your cropped JPG, PNG, or WebP signature image (up to 20 MB and 25 megapixels). Choose 'Detailed · larger model' (up to 473 MB first-run download on supported hardware, with automatic fallback to the 98 MB Standard model) for finer stroke retention.
corrections.proposedText: Open Clearcut on desktop Chrome or Edge and upload, drop, or paste your cropped JPG, PNG, or WebP signature image (up to 20 MB and 25 megapixels). 'Standard · original model (98 MB)' is the default; 'Detailed · larger model' swaps in larger weights (up to 473 MB first-run download on supported hardware, with automatic fallback to the 98 MB Standard model) and adds a focused second pass only when the detected subject occupies under 85% of the frame, so it may not run on a tightly cropped signature. Compare both modes against a dark background swatch before you export.
corrections.verification: runtime-test per R1-a, recording whether the refining stage appeared for each input framing.

evidence.note: MAX_REFINEMENT_AREA_RATIO = 0.85; findRefinementCrop returns null when cropArea >= imageArea * 0.85 or when the crop is under 32px on either axis.
createMaskRefinement returns undefined when no crop is found, so no second pass runs.
The refinement crop is taken from a copy scaled so the longest side is at most 1024px, then mapped back to full output resolution.
